title: Continuous Planar Isotropy and Euclidean Length: A Lean-Verified Characterization
description:
Version 0.2.0 of a Lean 4/Mathlib formalization investigating how planar symmetry constrains an initially unspecified length function. The project extends the original v0.1.0 conditional derivation of the coordinate Pythagorean theorem.

The main new result characterizes Euclidean length: for any function L on the real plane satisfying L(z,0) = |z|, the existence of a continuous additive linear action containing an oriented primitive quarter-turn and preserving L is equivalent to L(x,y) = sqrt(x^2 + y^2) for all real x and y. The forward implication derives axis reachability and reflection symmetry instead of assuming them. The converse provides an explicit trigonometric model. Additional Lean-verified counterexamples show why finite quarter-turn symmetry alone is insufficient.

The mathematical statements and proofs have passed Lean verification and independent Comparator checking, including mechanical verification through Palomar. These results are conditional on their stated hypotheses and do not establish historical novelty, axiom minimality, or derivation of the motion action from synthetic geometry.

Alessandro Odasso initiated the research question by asking OpenAI ChatGPT for an original proof of the Pythagorean theorem. The mathematical exposition and proposed argument were AI-generated using ChatGPT (GPT-6, High thinking effort), and the Lean formalization and subsequent extensions were AI-assisted. The word original describes the initial research prompt, not a substantiated claim of mathematical priority.
